title: Mandelbrot Set
body:
Evan's final project for this course. The set is defined by one iteration, run on the complex plane:

$$
z_0 = 0, \qquad z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c
$$

**$c$ is in the Mandelbrot set when this orbit stays bounded forever.** That is the entire
definition. One quadratic, iterated, and the question asked of every point $c$ in the plane is a
[[Complex Convergence]] question: bounded or divergent.

## The escape criterion

The saving fact: **if $|z_n| > 2$ for any $n$, the orbit is guaranteed to diverge.** Once past
radius 2 the squaring outruns the addition and the terms grow without bound. So divergence is
*detectable in finite time*.

Boundedness is not. If the orbit never escapes you never learn that it will not, you only run out of
patience. So the standard algorithm is:

```
for each pixel c:
    z = 0
    for i in 0..MAX_ITER:
        z = z*z + c
        if |z| > 2:
            colour by i and stop      # proved outside
    else:
        colour black                  # assumed inside
```

**The black region is a guess.** Every escaped point is a proof; no unescaped point is. Raising
`MAX_ITER` moves pixels out of the black, never into it, and the boundary is where that keeps
happening at any resolution.

That asymmetry is a semi-decidable problem, which is [[Undecidability]]'s material in
[[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]]: a procedure that halts and answers yes on every member of one
class and may run forever on the other, exactly like the halting problem's recogniser. **The
Mandelbrot set as computed is a recognisable set, not a decidable one**, and it is the most
photogenic example of that distinction in the degree. The colour bands people find beautiful are
literally a plot of *how long the semi-decision procedure took*.

## What it looks like and why

- The boundary is a fractal (the vault has no note for the term): self-similar under magnification,
  with small copies of the whole set appearing throughout it, and infinitely detailed at every
  scale. Its area is finite, its boundary has Hausdorff dimension 2.
- The self-similarity comes from the iteration being applied to its own output, which is
  [[Recursion]] in the mathematical sense: an unbounded structure generated by one rule with no
  special cases.
- **Trivial local rule, unbounded global structure** is the same phenomenon as
  [[Cellular Automata]] in [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]], where Rule 110 does the same trick
  with a lookup table of eight entries and turns out to be Turing complete.
- The set is connected, which is not obvious from the pictures: the visible islands are joined to
  the main body by filaments too thin to render.

## Related

- [[Julia Set]] is the same iteration with the roles of $z$ and $c$ swapped, and the Mandelbrot set
  is exactly the map of which Julia sets are connected.
- [[Complex Numbers]] and [[Polar Form]] for the squaring: $z^2$ doubles the argument
  and squares the modulus, which is why radius 2 is the escape threshold.
- Rendering it is embarrassingly parallel, one independent iteration per pixel, which makes it a
  standard benchmark for GPU and thread work.
